WWBN AVideo 12.4 through 29.7.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the ADs plugin deleteImage.json.php that allows authenticated users with custom ads to delete arbitrary files. Attackers can set the unvalidated is_regular_user parameter to another user's id or ../ sequences to delete other users' ads or files like videos/configuration.php, taking the site offline and re-exposing the installer.

WWBN AVideo 14.3 through 29.7.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows uploaders to inject scripts via the videoDownloadedLink value stored unescaped through objects/aVideoEncoder.json.php. Attackers can embed event-handler payloads in the URL host rendered as a Source tag in view/managerVideos_body.php, executing in administrator sessions to install plugin archives containing PHP.

WuzAPI through 1.1.0 contains a cross-tenant information disclosure vulnerability in the GetHistory handler that allows authenticated users to view other tenants' chat metadata. Attackers with message history enabled can request GET /chat/history with chat_jid=index to list every user's internal ID, stored chat JIDs, and last-message times.

weDevs ERP (WP ERP) through 1.17.11 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated employees to edit their own HR records because HRM AJAX handlers check erp_edit_employee instead of erp_manage_jobinfo. Attackers can post their own user_id with the My Profile nonce to change designation, reporting manager, pay rate, and employment type, or delete job history.

WWBN AVideo 29.1.0 through 29.7.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject markup through the channel About field rendered in feed/index.php. Attackers can store an unquoted event-handler payload that bypasses feedHtmlDescription() filtering and executes via rss-style.xsl for any visitor, including administrators, viewing the channel feed.

BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' unpublished draft page images by checking only PageView permission without draft status. Attackers can read drawio data via the base64 endpoint or rename, replace, or delete draft images by sequential ID to disclose or tamper with unpublished work.

blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.7 contains an insecure default configuration in its Docker Compose examples that sets MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes in database.env and publishes MariaDB on port 3306. Unauthenticated attackers reaching the Docker host on port 3306 can log in as root without a password to read, modify, or delete user accounts, blueprints, and all databases.

Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.21 and 1.7.x before 1.7.6 contains an IMAP command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject commands via CRLF in the _uid parameter when messages_cache is enabled. Attackers can lure logged-in victims into opening crafted GET links to mail/show or mail/get, executing IMAP commands that delete messages, change flags, or grant mailbox access via SETACL.

blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.6 contains an iframe injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to embed arbitrary third-party content by abusing the PeerTube video URL matcher in BlueprintService::findVideoProvider(). Attackers can set a blueprint video URL on an attacker-controlled host, which site.js loads in an unsandboxed iframe after consent, framing fake login forms or malware downloads.

Pre-account hijacking in the authentication flow in Lagarto Chivato 0.4.1 and earlier on Web allows remote unauthenticated attackers to take over arbitrary accounts via a password planted on an unregistered email address that becomes valid upon the victim’s first passwordless login.

A flaw in the automatic client-side encryption schema generation of the Mongoid ODM may cause values that an application declared for encryption to be written and stored as cleartext when more than one model is mapped onto the same storage location. No error or warning is raised. A party holding an ordinary read-only database account, with no access to the encryption key material, may then obtain those values in clear form.

A Ruby object-document mapper does not apply its automatic field-level encryption configuration to certain fields when the data model uses class inheritance. Values the application designated for encryption are written to the database in readable form without any error or warning. A database account holding only read access to the application's collections, and no access to the encryption key store, may obtain those values.

A local user with an ordinary account on the same host can place a file in a shared temporary location that the JDBC driver's native library loading routine will accept and load without verifying its origin. Loading the driver class in a Java application may then run code of that user's choosing inside the application process, which may result in disclosure or alteration of data held by that process or in the process becoming unavailable.

A flaw was found in cpio. A local user can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering a stack-based buffer overflow when creating archives in tar or ustar formats. When archiving files owned by users or groups with names exceeding 32 characters, cpio copies these names into fixed-size memory without verifying their length. This unbounded copy corrupts stack memory and causes the application to crash.

The MongoDB Node.js driver does not consistently enforce its permitted-host restriction during OIDC authentication. A bearer token produced by the embedding application's own login callback may therefore be transmitted to a host outside the configured set of permitted hosts, which may result in unintended disclosure of that credential. No database account is required; the party supplying the connection configuration needs only to influence the settings the application passes to the driver.

A MongoDB Rust Driver component that holds client-side field level encryption settings includes key management service credential material in its diagnostic formatting output without redaction. An application that records or displays this formatted output may place that material where a party with read access to the application's diagnostic output can see it, which may result in unintended disclosure of key material.

A deserialization type-restriction control in the BSON serialization component can be bypassed because the check used to recognize a class of compiler-generated types relies on an overly permissive heuristic rather than a precise identification. An unauthorized party able to supply BSON content that an application later deserializes into a loosely typed member can cause types outside the intended allow-list to be constructed and populated with unauthorized party-supplied values inside the consuming application. This can lead to unexpected object state and errors in downstream application logic. No elevated privileges beyond the ability to place unauthorized party-influenced content in the deserialization path are required.

Zipline 4.6.2 before 4.8.0 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade administrator-disabled MIME types by editing file metadata. Attackers can upload a permitted file, then set a disabled type such as text/html through PATCH /api/user/files/:id so /raw/:id serves that Content-Type.

Zipline 4.0.0 before 4.8.0 contains an upload filter bypass vulnerability that allows users with upload access to store blocked file types due to extension format mismatch. The upload and partial handlers compare dotted, case-sensitive extensions against undotted disabledExtensions entries, letting authenticated or permitted unauthenticated folder uploaders bypass administrator restrictions.

Zipline 4.3.2 before 4.8.0 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade throttling by spoofing X-Forwarded-For headers when core.trustProxy is enabled. Attackers can send a different X-Forwarded-For value per request to obtain fresh rate-limit buckets, enabling unlimited guessing of login passwords, TOTP codes, and file and URL passwords.

Zipline before 4.7.0 contains a race condition vulnerability that allows users to bypass invitation usage limits, upload storage quotas, and shortened-URL quotas through concurrent requests. Attackers can send overlapping registration, upload, or URL creation requests that pass checks against stale state, creating extra accounts and exceeding administrator-configured resource quotas.

Zipline before 4.6.5 contains a TOCTOU race condition in the POST /api/setup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to create multiple SUPERADMIN accounts by racing concurrent requests before the firstSetup flag is reset. Attackers can send simultaneous requests with spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers during the argon2 hashing window to gain full administrative control of the instance.

Zipline before 4.6.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in GET /api/server/folder/:id that allows unauthenticated attackers to list files in non-public upload-only folders. Attackers who know the folder UUID can supply the page query parameter to bypass the metadata-only early return and enumerate file names, IDs, MIME types, sizes, and view counts.

Zipline before 4.6.4 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to evade request limits by varying query strings or supplying the x-zipline-p-filename header. Attackers can append differing query parameters to login and file or short-link password verification endpoints to perform credential guessing beyond the intended rate limits.

Zipline through 4.6.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to read superadmin secrets because GET /api/users and GET /api/users/:id lack the canInteract check. Attackers can retrieve plaintext totpSecret and OAuth tokens to bypass 2FA and take over superadmin accounts, while any authenticated user can enumerate other users' folders via GET /api/user/folders.

Zipline from 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that logs sensitive environment variable values, such as OAUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, without redaction at startup. Attackers with access to system journal or docker logs can obtain OAuth2 client secrets and use them to exchange intercepted OAuth2 callbacks for valid tokens.

Zipline before 4.6.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in LocalDatasource that allows SUPERADMIN users to read or delete files outside the upload directory by importing records with traversal filenames. Attackers can trigger the unchecked range-read path with byte-range requests or set expired deletion times to delete files accessible to the Zipline process.

Zipline before 4.5.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the HighlightCode component that renders unescaped file content before highlight.js finishes loading. Authenticated attackers can upload text files containing HTML/JavaScript payloads that execute in viewers' browsers, enabling API calls such as account changes on the victim's behalf.

Zipline before 4.5.0 contains a stored open redirect vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set arbitrary short URL destinations by abusing missing scheme validation in POST /api/user/urls. Attackers can store javascript: URIs or attacker-controlled URLs as destinations, causing visitors of the trusted short link to be redirected to phishing or malware pages.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files by injecting traversal sequences via the x-zipline-file-extension header. Attackers can upload a file with a poisoned stored name and short expiry so LocalDatasource deletion removes chosen files, causing denial of service or data loss.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary server files by abusing a fallback treating the :id parameter as a datasource key. Attackers can send encoded traversal sequences in the :id of GET /api/user/files/:id/raw to escape the Local datasource uploads directory and read files like /etc/shadow.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to execute commands as root by supplying an unvalidated InternetGatewayDevice.User.{i}.Username value. Attackers can send a SetParameterValues request with shell metacharacters that set_UserUsername() in obuspa_system.lua passes to os.execute(), gaining root command execution.

Glance from 0.7.9 before 0.8.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious extension endpoints to inject javascript: URLs via the Widget-Title-URL response header. Attackers controlling an extension endpoint can execute script when users click the widget title, reading dashboard pages through same-origin requests and exfiltrating content.

An integer underflow in Zephyr's IPv4 option handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to read stack memory. When replying to an ICMP Echo Request that carries an IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp option, icmpv4_update_record_route() and icmpv4_update_time_stamp() in subsys/net/ip/icmpv4.c compute the length of the already recorded data as ptr - ptr_offset in uint8_t arithmetic. The attacker-controlled Pointer field is checked against the option length but not against the RFC 791 minimum (4 for Record Route, 5 for Timestamp), so a smaller value wraps the length to up to 252 bytes. net_pkt_write() then reads past the 40-byte opt_data stack buffer and up to 213 bytes of stack memory, which can include stack and heap pointers, are returned in the ICMP Echo Reply. A single packet triggers the leak and the device does not crash, so it can be repeated. Devices built with CONFIG_NET_IPV4_HDR_OPTIONS, which CONFIG_NET_IPV4_IGMP selects, are affected.

A type allow-list bypass in the BSON serialization library of the MongoDB C# Driver allows a type-restriction check to be circumvented when polymorphic data is deserialized into loosely typed members. An unauthorized party who can supply or plant BSON/JSON data that the application later deserializes can cause the application process to instantiate .NET types outside the intended allow-list and populate them with unauthorized party-controlled values. In applications that contain a suitable gadget type, this can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the application, with corresponding loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability. No special privileges beyond the ability to introduce data the application reads are required.

A vulnerability was found in tjake Jlama up to 0.8.4/0.9.0-beta. Affected by this vulnerability is the function SafeTensorIndex.loadWeights of the file jlama-core/src/main/java/com/github/tjake/jlama/safetensors/SafeTensorIndex.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument weight_map results in path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A flaw was found in freeradius. An improper length validation in the EAP-FAST module allows a stack-based buffer overflow during session ticket processing. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by sending a specially crafted handshake request, causing the server process to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

Improper neutralization of CRLF sequences ('CRLF injection') vulnerability in ibi WebFOCUS.

This issue affects WebFOCUS: 9.1, from 9.2 through 7, and from 9.3 through 7.

Backup Migration before 2.1.8 for WordPress contains a path traversal vulnerability in its PclZip restore fallback that allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary file write when an administrator restores a malicious backup archive on a server lacking the PHP zip extension. Attackers can craft a zip archive with entry names containing ".." sequences, which PclZip's extract() processes without the PCLZIP_OPT_EXTRACT_DIR_RESTRICTION option, writing a PHP file outside the intended extraction directory into the web-servable tree to achieve remote code execution.

PapaParse before 5.7.1 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to cause denial of service by submitting delimiter-free quoted CSV input to Papa.parse(). Attackers can supply a single-column quoted CSV with no delimiters, triggering repeated full-buffer indexOf scans per row that grow quadratically with input size, exhausting CPU and blocking the Node.js event loop or freezing a browser tab.

The
third-party RMM+ extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect uses a static API
secret by default. The value can be changed by an administrator; however,
environments retaining the default value may allow unauthorized access to
extension API functionality, including the ability to send commands to managed
agents. This issue is specific to the third-party extension and does not affect
the ScreenConnect server or client.





Scope: This issue affects the third-party RMM+
extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect. Deployments without the extension are
not affected. ScreenConnect server or client software are not impacted.

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users with build configuration permission to read files on the build worker by supplying unvalidated dockerfile_path and build context values. Attackers can set traversal or absolute paths such as /etc/passwd via the CI configuration endpoint, then trigger a build to disclose file contents in the build log.

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary files by supplying traversal sequences in Additional Manifest file paths. Attackers can enter paths like ../../../../etc/passwd so the renderer embeds file contents in generated manifests and logs, exposing configuration files and service-account tokens.

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to attach another application's environment to their service by supplying a foreign project_env_id. Attackers can configure CI and trigger builds and deployments through the component env endpoints using the other application's configuration, registries and deployment infrastructure.

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 lacks rate limiting on password-reset OTP verification, allowing unauthenticated attackers to brute force 6-digit OTPs. Attackers can initiate a reset and submit unthrottled guesses to the check_otp endpoint, resetting the target's password and taking over the account.

Huginn before 2026.11.09 contains an information exposure vulnerability in JqAgent that allows authenticated users to read the server process environment because the jq child process inherits it. Attackers who can create, configure or dry-run a JqAgent can supply a filter using env or $ENV to disclose APP_SECRET_TOKEN, database, SMTP and OAuth secrets.

Huginn from 2026.09.09 before 2026.11.09 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability because OutboundProxy.configure! applies the egress proxy only to Faraday and Typhoeus. Authenticated users can configure JiraAgent or WeiboPublishAgent to send HTTParty, open-uri or Net::HTTP requests directly to internal services, with JiraAgent returning response data as events.

Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to upload SVG or HTML attachments with an attacker-chosen content type. Attackers can send the same-origin /api/attachments/read URL, served inline with an empty Content-Security-Policy, to run script with the victim's session and perform API actions.

Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to take over other users' collections by supplying an updateId to the createOrUpdateCollection GraphQL mutation. Attackers who know a collection id can trigger ownership reassignment without checks, read its items, rewrite metadata, and evict the original owner and collaborators.

Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to revoke other users' access links by supplying an arbitrary accessLinkId. Attackers can obtain access link ids from public share URLs and revoke them without ownership checks, breaking shared access for all link users.

Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, contain an improper path equivalence flaw in VirtualFileFactory.canonicalisePath that bypasses mount-level access policy. Authenticated users can supply paths with duplicate separators or dot segments to route operations to a less restrictive parent mount and read or write files the child mount denies.

BuildAdmin 1.0.1 through 2.3.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to store javascript: URLs in the admin operation log via the X-Rewrite-URL header. When an administrator clicks the log entry's url open button, the script runs in the backend origin and steals the adminInfo token from localStorage, enabling account takeover.

Rustrak before 0.26.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows users with integrations update permission to send requests to arbitrary destinations by supplying routing_override.url to POST /api/integrations/{id}/test. Attackers can target loopback, private-network and cloud metadata addresses with custom headers and redirects followed, reading non-2xx response bodies returned in the API response.

A flaw was found in SSSD's conversion of X.509 certificate RSA public keys to SSH keys. Missing size checks before copying RSA components into fixed-size stack buffers can cause a stack buffer overflow. An attacker able to supply a certificate with oversized RSA components that passes the configured certificate checks can cause denial of service and corrupt SSH responder memory.

A flaw was found in SSSD's PAM responder on builds with the JSON PAM extension enabled. A local attacker can submit a crafted authentication request containing a non-string OAuth2 code value. Missing JSON type validation leads to a NULL pointer dereference, terminating the PAM responder and disrupting SSSD-backed authentication.

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment return Submodel Elements that the caller is not authorized to read from `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/submodel-elements`.



If an access rule grants READ on a single Submodel Element through a `$sme` `REFERABLE` object, the list route returns every element of that Submodel, including its value, as soon as one element matches the caller's rules. The single-element route and the full Submodel read enforce the same rule and deny access to the other elements. An authenticated caller with a READ grant for one element of a Submodel can therefore read all other elements of that Submodel.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

A code injection vulnerability in promzard’s template-loading functionality allows an attacker who can control property names in the context object (ctx) to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the Node.js process. The library inserts context property names into a generated function’s parameter list without validation or escaping and evaluates the resulting source using `vm.runInThisContext()`. A crafted property name can escape the parameter list and inject JavaScript code, even when the template file is fully trusted.

Unverified ownership of the default cluster log location in the EMR module in AWS SDK for pandas (awswrangler) from 1.1.0 before 3.18.0 might allow remote actors to read Amazon EMR cluster logs, including job step output, via a pre-created S3 bucket.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 3.18.0 or later. Users who can't upgrade immediately should pass an explicit log location, or create the default EMR log bucket in their own account in each region they use.

A vulnerability was found in Governikus AusweisApp Mobile up to 2.5.5. This impacts an unknown function of the component StartPAOSResponse Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument ResultMessage results in cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 2.6.0 will fix this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

SOGo before 5.12.13 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the server connect to arbitrary internal host:port destinations by supplying a user-controlled URL to the Calendar/addWebCalendar endpoint. Attackers can trigger a reload of the subscribed web calendar via the reload endpoint and distinguish response outcomes such as connection failures, timeouts, authentication prompts, or invalid content to probe the internal network from the server's position.

MLflow before 3.18.0 using the FileStore backend contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files outside the intended run directory by supplying a malicious model_id parameter to the log outputs API. Attackers can exploit the unvalidated model_id containing ../ sequences via the POST /api/3.0/mlflow/runs/outputs endpoint to create directories and write a meta.yaml file at arbitrary filesystem locations, limited only by the server account's permissions. FileStore was the default backend before 3.7.0 and is opt-in afterward through MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE.

AppFlowy Cloud through 0.9.64 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace members to upload blobs with unvalidated Content-Type values that are later served inline without a Content-Disposition header or authentication on the retrieval route. Attackers can upload a text/html or image/svg+xml blob via put_blob_handler, which is then rendered as an active same-origin document through the unauthenticated get_blob_handler endpoint and cached immutably for one year, enabling persistent script execution against any visitor who accesses the URL.

Image CAPTCHA for Contact Form 7 and WPForms through 3.3.29 contains a CAPTCHA bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to defeat the anti-automation control by exploiting a hardcoded static answer in the Contact Form 7 integration. Attackers can submit kc_captcha=kc_human to pass validation in cf7ic_check_if_spam() on every protected form, enabling automated contact-form spam and abuse of actions gated only by this CAPTCHA.

datamodel-code-generator before 0.84.0 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying a malicious JSON Schema with a crafted x-python-type annotation containing a string ast.Constant node in a subscript slice position, which bypasses validation in parse_python_type_annotation and _python_type_expr_from_ast. Attackers can embed malicious Python expressions such as __import__ calls within quoted string literals in the generated source code, which Pydantic v2 evaluates as a ForwardRef via eval() during model_rebuild(), resulting in arbitrary code execution on developer workstations, CI/CD pipelines, or applications that generate and import the produced models at runtime.

Xiaomi Mi Browser Android Application (com.mi.globalbrowser) before 14.66.0-gn contains a path traversal vulnerability in the exported ThirdDocViewerActivity component, where CopyExternalFile.copyFromUri() copies content provider streams using an unsanitized filename from the _display_name column without basename reduction or canonical-path checks. A zero-permission co-resident malicious application can supply a crafted content provider with a _display_name containing .. sequences to make the browser write attacker-controlled bytes to an arbitrary path within its external storage directory, escaping the intended cache_docs staging location without requiring user interaction.

MultiVendorX plugin for WordPress before 5.0.22 contains a broken access control vulnerability in the /wp-json/multivendorx/v1/stores REST route that allows authenticated vendors to access administrative flag handlers due to the store_owner role possessing the edit_stores capability and missing per-store ownership checks. Attackers can exploit the insecure direct object reference in the visitorMap handler and other flag handlers to retrieve other stores' contact emails, pending withdrawal amounts, onboarding and registration data, deactivation reasons, and visitor analytics, resulting in a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.

Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains a missing ownership check vulnerability in the readAppMonitoring tRPC procedure that allows authenticated attackers to access container metrics belonging to other organizations by supplying an arbitrary appName. Attackers can query getApplicationStats with any application name, including the fixed "dokploy" control-plane service name, to read CPU, memory, network I/O, and block I/O metrics for containers they do not own on self-hosted multi-tenant instances.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability exists in the web user interface of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. Several web UI pages copy request parameter values into the HTML response without correct contextual output encoding. A remote attacker can craft a link that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the OpenNMS origin when an authenticated user opens it. The script runs in the victim's browser with the victim's session, so the attacker can read page data and send same-origin requests as the victim. The fix encodes the affected request values. On pages that use AngularJS, the fix also stops client-side template evaluation of the reflected values.



The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

An argument injection vulnerability exists in the ad-hoc RRD graph feature of multiple versions of OpenNMS Meridian and Horizon. The ad-hoc graph endpoint (GET /graph/graph.png?adhoc=true) copies request parameters into the rrdtool command line without validation. A low-privileged authenticated user (ROLE_USER or ROLE_DASHBOARD) can insert extra rrdtool arguments. An injected --daemon argument makes the server connect to an attacker-chosen address, which is a server-side request forgery. An injected DEF statement reads a local RRD file by absolute path. The command runs through exec with an argument array and no shell, so arbitrary operating system command execution is not possible. The fix validates the ad-hoc graph parameters against allowlists.



The solution is to upgrade to Meridian 2024.3.15, 2025.0.12, 2026.0.2 and Horizon 36.0.6 or newer. Meridian and Horizon installation instructions state that they are intended for installation within an organization's private networks and should not be directly accessible from the Internet.

Performing a manipulation of the argument ANON_ACCESS results in improper initialization. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in lanyulei ferry 1.0.0-beta.1/1.0.0. Affected is an unknown function of the file middleware/auth.go of the component JWT Validation. The manipulation results in improper authentication. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in SourceCodester Smart Attendance System with QR Code Scanner 1.0. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file reset_password.php. This manipulation of the argument Username causes cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

A vulnerability was identified in SourceCodester Food Ordering System 1.0. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file admin/update_food.php of the component Admin Image Handler. Such manipulation of the argument cmd leads to unrestricted upload. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

A flaw has been found in Cairo-dock Glx-Dock 3.4.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file bg_forum.php of the component href Attribute Handler. This manipulation of the argument f causes cross site scripting. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.
